body:
CORRECTED 2026-08-24, same night it was filed. **The first version of this
finding was wrong** and is preserved at the bottom so the error is visible.

## What is actually true

A deletion does NOT trigger an annotation PATCH by itself. It waits for a
carrier: the next time the device has some other annotation change **in that
same book** to upload, the PATCH goes out and the deletion rides along.

Measured end to end on the operator's Clara BW:

    05:30:40  highlight A authored on a zero-annotation book
    05:31:53  A reaches the server (hidden=0)              <- create propagates in ~1s
    05:36:06  A deleted via the device's Annotations panel
              device writes Hidden='true' and CLEARS SyncTime
    ...
    23 hours pass, many device syncs, A still hidden=0 on the server
    ...
    00:28     highlight B authored in the SAME book
    04:28:49  PATCH goes out; B is created AND A's deletion is applied
              server: A hidden=1 content_revision=4
              device: A's Bookmark row is now GONE entirely

So the deletion did eventually land, and once acknowledged Nickel removes the
row rather than keeping a tombstone.

## The defect that remains, stated at its real size

**A highlight the reader deleted stays live on the server for as long as they
make no further annotation in that book.** Measured here: 23 hours and still
counting until an unrelated highlight forced it out. For a book someone
finishes and never annotates again, that is indefinite.

Consequences:
- The deleted highlight keeps showing in CWNG's web reader.
- More seriously, with design section 11.2 now closed, server-to-device
  writeback is viable. Writeback against a server set that still holds these
  un-uploaded deletions would push the deleted highlight **back onto the
  device**. The user deletes a highlight, and it returns.

This is not CWNG's bug to fix in the device: Nickel decides when to PATCH. It
IS CWNG's problem to be robust against, and the writeback design needs to say
what it does about a book whose last known device state may be stale in exactly
this way.

## What the earlier version got wrong, and why

It claimed deletions **never** propagate, on the strength of a positive control
that looked strong and was not: the operator created a dogear about sixteen
hours after the deletion, in a DIFFERENT book, and it synced in a second. That
proves the device-to-server path was alive. It proves nothing about the deleted
highlight's book, because **the annotation PATCH is per-book** — a create in
book X is not a carrier for a delete in book Y.

The evidence was equally consistent with "deletions never propagate" and with
"deletions need a same-book carrier", and the wrong one was chosen. The
discriminating test was cheap and is what settled it: author a second
annotation **in the same book** and see whether the pending deletion rides out.

Note also that the "tombstone, not a row delete" framing was only half right.
`Hidden='true'` with a cleared `SyncTime` is a *pending-upload* marker, not a
durable tombstone; it resolves to a genuine row deletion once the server
acknowledges. Anything reading `Bookmark` should still filter `Hidden`, because
the pending window can last indefinitely.

---
ORIGINAL (WRONG) CLAIM, kept deliberately: "A highlight deleted on the Kobo
never reaches the server, so it stays live in the web reader and would be
resurrected by writeback." Confidence came from a 23-hour window plus a
cross-book control. Both were real observations; the conclusion drawn from them
was not.

---
PROVENANCE OF THE ROWS, added 2026-08-24 so nobody miscounts this later.

Three `hidden=1` rows in book 540 are **mine**, authored and deleted during this
investigation. They are NOT operator data and must not be counted as evidence of
user-visible loss:

    665557e8-ffd2-485d-890e-e6c13124e44d   ' son'    book 540
    8d7d2a6d-dc7c-44d9-8643-6b2949ae9e39   ' son'    book 540
    789e11f0-6511-462e-9614-f465fef39592   'Vivek '  book 540

Book 540 is back to 0 live annotations and the library to 638.

This matters because a separate reconciliation of `hidden=1`-on-server /
absent-on-device rows initially read as independent corroboration of the
corrected model, and up to three of its four rows are these test annotations.
That reconciliation is therefore **mostly this same experiment measured from a
second angle**, not a separate line of evidence, and it should not be cited as
one.

**What the finding does rest on** is the 23-hour observation, which is a direct
measurement and does not depend on that reconciliation:

    05:30:40  665557e8 authored
    05:31:53  reaches the server
    05:36:06  deleted on the device; Hidden='true', SyncTime cleared
    ...       23 hours, many device syncs, still hidden=0 on the server
    04:28:49  an unrelated highlight is authored in the SAME book; the PATCH
              carries the pending deletion out with it

⚠️ **And the honest limit of the carrier half.** The rows that demonstrate the
carrier mechanism were authored and deleted inside one active session, in a book
being actively worked in — which is exactly the condition under which the model
predicts a deletion gets carried out. So they establish the mechanism under
favourable conditions and say much less about the interesting case: a book the
reader finishes, deletes a highlight in, and never annotates again. That case is
evidenced by the 23-hour gap alone, and 23 hours is a lower bound, not a limit.
title: A highlight deleted on the Kobo is not uploaded until some OTHER annotation in the same book is, so it can stay live on the server indefinitely
